utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom, especially to those I hardly can see but those are always there to assist us. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we continue the examination of the present witness, I would like to turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, after we return to open session and before I recommence cross-examination, might I raise an issue --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yesterday, Mr. President, you asked if it was contested by the Defence [sic] that there were daily combats, and I said it was not. I seek to amend that to rather than daily, frequent combats, because there is evidence that there was from time to time some ceasefires through the indictment period where the level of combat activity either diminished or, in particular, after Markale, virtually ceased for a period of time. What is agreed is that there were frequent combats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I understood, but I perhaps have to check it perhaps first whether it was combat on a daily basis. In view of the testimony of the witness, I would say that this specifically related to the time when he was at the front line. That is how I understood the testimony, and that is also how I understood my own question. But if there is any problem with that, the Defence will then have an opportunity to come back to this. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, just to make sure that everything is clear, I believe that I think the Prosecution made a lapsus lingua in page 2 line 2 just to clarify things in the transcript, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, it is contested by the Prosecution, rather than by the Defence. Madam Registrar could you please escort Mr. DP6 into the courtroom and since facial distortion is in effect, I take it that he will not be visible for the outside world when going to his seat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr. DP6. Mr. DP6, may I remind you again that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave the day before yesterday. Your cross-examination will now be continued by Mr. Ierace. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. President. Would Madam Registrar have at hand Defence Exhibit 1761, that is the photograph that I showed to the witness yesterday. If it is not on hand immediately, I can move on to some other questions. That is the photograph from the high-rise showing the car park in the mid-ground. The witnesses marked some buildings with circles and numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I have it now as P3752.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, does it appear to you that this photograph was taken recently, and certainly after the end of 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: During the period from September 1992 until August of 1994, there were no trees in that area. Is that correct? That is, the trees had few branches and few leaves --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to this question. The photograph shows a considerable number of trees, in fact wood. So perhaps we could have a more accurate question. Such-and-such a tree, because there were so many trees in this photograph, that the question seems impossible to answer, as it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Some of the trees visible on the photograph, one might wonder whether they could have grown that high in such a short period. So would you please be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. That is why I qualified the question by saying "the trees had few branches and few leaves." But I will rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The trees that were there during the indictment period had been --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to the phrasing. The witness doesn't know what the indictment period is. He doesn't know it. He can't know it. He has to be given dates so that he can answer. It is a formal objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Between September 1992 and August 1994 the trees that were in the area shown by the photograph had few branches and even in the warmer months, had few leaves. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have to object to this kind of question. This is about all the trees, and how can the witness know this because all of the trees -- if all of the trees in this photograph had few branches. It seems to me that this is a very meaningless question, really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do agree with the Defence, Mr. Ierace, that it is Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. such a wide area --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am happy to withdraw the question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In spite of the fact that it has been answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, in the area where you were operating between September 1992 and August 1994, were there civilians living?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilians lived there deep into Nedzarici, those that didn't have to go anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What do you mean by "deep into Nedzarici"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, for instance, from the first line, from the front line, about 100 metres, since Nedzarici was surrounded, then they had to live there about in the centre of Nedzarici, in the middle, because they couldn't live on the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So up to 100 metres from the front line on your side, there were civilians living. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did they have -- I think you said yesterday there was not electricity and, therefore, there was not water from time to time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that there was no electricity and, therefore, there was no water. I also said that we had a well from which we drew water.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. What did the civilians use in order to keep warm in the colder months?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the cold months there was gas. So we used gas as fuel for heating.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did they -- sorry. Go on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. And also, we had some firewood.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: But there was no need for the civilians to chop down the trees to produce wood for cooking and heating. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course there was need for that. There was need for that. When there was no gas, then civilians had to use something to heat themselves with.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Earlier you told us there was gas for heating. Do you now mean that there was not always gas for heating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did that not mean that the trees on your territory were harvested for wood for heating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you couldn't cut the trees down because they were -- above us were high-rise buildings; none of us dared to go near and cut it off.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where there were trees obstructing your view of important parts of the territory of the enemy, did you and your subordinates take steps to eliminate them through gunfire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We couldn't get to the trees to eliminate them -- to eliminate the trees. Because a moment ago I said that above us, there were high-rise buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which is why I asked you if gunfire was used to achieve that objective.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We didn't open fire because of the trees. We only opened fire in case of attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you understand the question? I am asking you whether gunfire was used to eliminate the cover provided by trees where important parts of the enemy territory was protected from sight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, how could you get rid of branches of a tree by gunfire? I don't understand. I don't know how you can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I suggest to you that bursts of gunfire can eliminate branches from trees. Do you disagree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We didn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Okay. You told us yesterday that before the -- at some stage before the conflict, you had been a permanent member of the JNA. Between what years were you in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't say that I was a permanent member.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, can the Prosecution please quote the line and page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am happy to do that, that is, find the reference to the witness saying he had been in the JNA. But in the meantime, I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I went to do my service in 1975. And I did my service for 15 months.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And is that where you gained some expertise with anti-aircraft artillery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I note my friend is on his feet, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to know, it is not my recollection that this witness said anything whatsoever, but perhaps I am mistaken. That's why I ask for quotation -- for the reference. I don't know whether he mentioned anti-aircraft artillery. I remember the shelling, but I don't remember the anti-aircraft. So perhaps if I could have the reference, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He did it on the first or the beginning of the second day. It is --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If I could assist, Mr. President. Firstly, the question did not say that he did, but as it happens he did, and the page number is 13864 at line 21, the reference to the witness being in the JNA is on the same page at line 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, in relation to anti-aircraft artillery --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. I remember well what I said. You asked me if I had served in the army and also what my military specialty was. So I said that was I light anti-aircraft artillery when I was serving -- when I was doing my military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Actually, it was the Defence who asked you that, not me. Now, in relation to anti-aircraft artillery, is that a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, of course, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that a weapon which is intended to place a number of exploding rounds over a large area in the path of aircraft?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is there a means of operating that weapon so that the barrel moves as it fires in order to spray rounds over a large area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand. What do you mean, "over a large area"?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The objective is not to fire successive rounds along the same -- exactly the same path, but rather for each round to go in a slightly different direction. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I was in the army, I was taught how to use an anti-aircraft cannon in order to hit an aircraft.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you try to repeat the question in such a way that the witness clearly understands what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you fire an anti-aircraft gun, bullets leave the barrel in quick succession, that is, there is a burst of fire that comes out of the barrel. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And the idea is not that each bullet goes exactly in the same direction, but rather bullets go in slightly different directions in order to create that wall of exploding rounds in front of the aircraft. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With an anti-aircraft cannon, when you are firing it, of course you press the pedal -- or I had forgotten how you are supposed to do Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that. Then the bullets are going from three different barrels and they are going one after the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. As you press the pedal, does that move the gun across an arch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well that -- you can stop that, you can put a brake on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. When you do cause the gun to move as it fires, if that is used against ground forces, it becomes an area weapon, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I learned in the army how to use it against aircraft, but for area forces, for land forces, I...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please finish your answer. For land forces what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And against land forces, I was not taught that. I only was trained to use it against aircraft.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you have any difficulty with the idea of using a weapon like that against land forces? Is there any problem with that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not a military strategist.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am objecting for the following reason. The witness just said that he did not learn and that he was not taught that this cannon can be used against land forces. Now, the following thing is that Mr. Ierace is addressing the witness, did you, do you have any difficulty and so on now, contrary to what the witness just said. So he cannot ask a question like this because the witness just said that he did not know that it was used as a land weapon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the question was rather hypothetical. Then you never used, Mr. DP6, anti-aircraft guns against -- on land, not against aircraft? Am I correct in understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We never used anti-aircraft cannons for targets on land in the army. While in the war, I didn't even have an opportunity to see an anti-aircraft cannon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you give it ever some thought on what the effect would be of using such a weapon, even if you did not do it yourself, in land warfare?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You also told us yesterday that you and your force obtained some weapons from the JNA barracks in Nedzarici, that you would go there in groups of 10 or 15. Is that correct? Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said that there was someone in the barracks. Would that person give you the guns?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were some people there; I didn't even know them. And then when 10 people arrived to take the weapons, they would return to the line, and then the next group would come.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And I take it that with the guns --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was an elderly man. I don't know what his name was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: With the guns, you also received presumably ammunition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And you told us -- how many groups were there that went? How many groups of 10 or 15 people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Seven or eight. I do say six, seven groups, as far as the front line was at which I was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And those troops left with M-48 rifles, semi-automatic, automatic rifles, and semi-automatic machine-guns. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that in relation to uniforms, that usually a number of you had JNA uniforms, some were civilian clothes, but then camouflage uniforms arrived. When did they arrive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wouldn't know exactly. Sometime in the autumn at about this time of year. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So about October of 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, thereabouts. I am not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were they winter uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They were olive/green/grey two-piece uniforms, the jacket and the trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where were they made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know where they came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the barracks, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: These were new uniforms weren't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they were both secondhand because in the former system, the troops had the uniforms, and when the troops pulled out, the uniforms stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. So were they JNA uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So from somewhere you and your troops all received winter uniforms ex-JNA, in October of 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, once the ammunition that you received from he JNA barracks ran out, I take it you were resupplied, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were supplied with ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At that stage, in October of 1992, did you regard yourself as a member of the Sarajevo Romanija Corp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Had you met General Galic by then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Had you heard of General Galic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I didn't hear about General Galic for a very long time. I don't even know when was it that I heard of him. Perhaps when I returned from this spa in Arandjelovac after my wounding.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In October 1993, is that when you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, after I was wounded, I don't know when it was that they heard, but it was then that I heard about General Galic, then -- I mean, when I returned from the spa.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever meet General Galic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You never -- you have never met General Galic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Have you ever seen General Galic before you appeared in this courtroom, in the flesh?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did General Mladic ever, between September 1992 and August 1994, go to Nedzarici? In other words, did you ever see him there between those dates?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you receive --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object because the question contained two elements. On one hand, whether General Mladic had visited or not Nedzarici; and secondly, whether the witness saw him. And now I do not know whether it is of any use to talk about General Mladic, but I object to the form of question which is a two-fold question and therefore the witness is unable to answer it directly

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was specified after first -- the question being whether General Mladic ever went to Nedzarici. It was then specified whether the witness saw him in Nedzarici. Would you answer the question: Did you ever see in the time period just mentioned, General Mladic in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, just in relation to ammunition for the small arms, and by that I mean up to and including machine-guns, did that ammunition come in boxes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It came -- some of it came in boxes, some of it came looser. I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. don't know. All I know is that it came.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, what do you mean you don't know, given that you were the company commander, how the ammunition arrived? Did it come just in boxes or in some other form?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ammunition came both in boxes and loose, that is, in soft board boxes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Either way, it came in boxes, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were crates, those army crates, and there were also some boxes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, where was, in what places was that ammunition manufactured according to the markings on the boxes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object. I object. I do not see that in the previous line of questioning the fact emanated that the crates were marked. I can well imagine a carton box which said Coca-Cola or something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, could you perhaps -- if you would like to ask the witness, first ask about the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Boxes of ammunition, I suggest to you, would have had markings on them as to their type and place of manufacture, at least the country of manufacture. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what it said on the crates and boxes. All I know is that we got the ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You at least had to look at the boxes to make sure they were the appropriate gauge of ammunition, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I opened the box and I see what the calibre is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I see. In relation to small arms, again, rifles, pistols, machine-guns, did you receive any fresh equipment up until August 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might the witness be shown again the map that he marked yesterday in cross-examination. I think that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps that could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yesterday you marked the brigade and battalion headquarters, and you indicated - and correct me if I am wrong - that they were the positions from the September 1992 throughout the period up until August of 1994. Is that the position? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The position you indicated for the battalion headquarters, I think you said that the headquarters stayed there from September 1992 until August of 1994. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did the battalion headquarters remain in that same -- remain in its position indicated on the map throughout the same period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The battalion command, I have said it, I know it was in Nedzarici until the 20th of February, 1993, and then I was wounded. When I was wounded, the battalion commander moved to Kasindolska Street -- but I don't know the date, because I was not there -- and stayed in Kasindolska until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does that street appear on the map, and if so, could you point to it with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the ELMO can pan back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here it is. Kasindolska. Like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, you told us that you were a company commander up until February of 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was your command headquarters in the same position throughout the period that you were a company commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on Lukavicka Cesta.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: First, with the pointer, would you indicate the position of the company headquarters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The company headquarters was somewhere -- somewhere here, in the middle between the first and the last position.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What type of building was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a house with some upper floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is necessary to show for the transcript that the witness pointed at a line which he himself drew as a continuous line and the middle of this line, because otherwise we won't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it will be marked in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was that house anywhere near the -- I withdraw that. How far was the house from the nearest building in the complex of the Institute for Blind Children, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For blind children, it was some 80 maybe 100 metres from the Institute for the Blind to the company headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please take a --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From here to here. That's about 80 to 150 -- well, I am not sure. About 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you now please take a black pen and with the black pen place a cross to indicate the position of the company headquarters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What about a blue pen, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I forgot, Mr. President. A blue pen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A blue pen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To the left of the cross, please place the letter "C."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And then underneath the cross, but avoiding writing over the black indicated front line, please write the initials "CHY."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the map could stay there for the moment. Well -- no, perhaps the map could be withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In any military -- in any armed combat, high ground is particularly valued. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us about how the ABiH took advantage of the high structures on their side of the confrontation line --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- and you also said in relation to your side that the Theological Institute was a high building, not as high, but a high building. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, four floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do apologise. Perhaps the usher could return the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: With the pointer -- withdraw that. Yesterday you marked the front line and in particular, as I understand it, the portion of the front line which was the responsibility of your company. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: With the pointer, could you slowly outline the entire territory which was the responsibility for your company.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I showed it to you yesterday, and I drew it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, you showed us the front line. But did that territory -- how far back from the front line was the territory that was occupied in particular by your company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My company was right next to the Lukavicka Cesta. Here, in these Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. houses, as I marked them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Well, if you had walked say 300 metres back from the front line, that is, towards the south-west, would there have been members of your company there as well or were they confined to the front line and the immediately adjacent area to the front line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The soldiers were always on the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In the area of Nedzarici occupied by the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, in terms of the highest buildings, there was the Theological Institute. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object. And the foundation for it is purely semantic. We have not accepted that term "aggressor" and, therefore, I do not think that we can accept the term "occupied" which does not -- means occupation as in some historical example that we already heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, may I take it that under the control, would there as well this is also considered to be sensitive?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Apart from the Theological Institute, what were the other tall buildings in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Come on, we didn't have any tall buildings apart from the Theological Faculty on the front line, and we had old people's home and the Centre for the Blind. Those were the tallest buildings in Nedzarici, I mean, because it was all private houses there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, were all of those private houses occupied by civilians between September 1992 and August 1994, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. Not all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In your company --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the front line -- on the front line there were no civilians. I said it last time a moment ago that some were about 100 metres in the depth of Nedzarici territory, there were still some civilians who had nowhere to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: By the end of 1992, how many troops were there in your company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until the end of 1992, I don't know the exact number. I think we were -- when I was wounded, that was 1993, we were some 118 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, in terms of equipment that your company had, how many mortars did you have by February 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One. The 60 one, 60 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many snipers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had no snipers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many snipers were operating on your part of the front line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not aware of any.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object. The witness has just said that there were no snipers, and then the next question asks him again how many of them were there at the front line. The witness knows only that front lines; he said there were no snipers. So it is an admissible to ask him a question like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...the question was about the company; the second was on that part of the front line in which the witness testified that only part of that front line was within his company. But the question has been answered. So, Mr. Ierace, I think there is no need to continue. The witness has testified that there were no snipers in his company, and that -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I certainly didn't eliminate the distinct possibility that snipers could have been brought in from other companies to operate on his portion of the front line, and that was what I had in mind with that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many snipers were there in the Ilidza Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't. And I don't know if there were any at all, because I was at this line here, and there were none, I am sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am sorry. But once again, these type of questions seems to me of a questionable form. The first question -- and I am talking now about the Ilidza Brigade, The first question should be whether the witness was aware of any snipers, and only then to ask him how many of them. And the question obviously is -- takes for granted that there were any snipers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...were these leading elements in the questioning are allowed. On the other hand, Mr. Ierace I do not always know -- I do not know whether it -- let me express myself in a different way. Sometimes leading the witness too much could result in losing a lot of information on the basis of his knowledge. So, although leading the witness is certainly not prohibited, I think in a system like ours, it might sometimes be of more assistance to give a better view on the basis of the knowledge of the witness rather than getting a certain answer from him. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, you have told us that you had one mortar and that it was a 62 millimetre. What other equipment did you have in your company, apart from --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 60 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What other equipment did you have in your company, apart from small arms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: None. Infantry weapons and the 60.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you returned in October 1993, what were your duties from then until August of 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I returned to the battalion after the severe wounding that I had sustained, I started working in the rear, food and the like.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At any stage between October 1993 and August 1994, did you go to the front line that you marked on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not really. Now and then.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because everybody had his duties, his assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What were the duties that you had that required you to go to the front line in that period, that part of the front line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, to go to that part of the front line, mostly was when food was being distributed, tins and the like. And I also went because I was the first company commander, and I wanted to see my comrades at arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Who took over control of the company after you in February 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jovo Sehovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did he stay there until at least August 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jovo you mean, yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: He remained in control of the company, in charge of the company, until that time, at least?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The food that you distributed was prepared where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was prepared in a kitchen at Ilidza, and then it was taken to two certain locations where people came to fetch it and then to get to the front line going -- using trenches and moving between houses and behind the screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, coming back to the operations of your company between -- up until February of 1993, did you come under fire from snipers in the high-rise buildings opposite to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there was sniper fire and all kinds of fire, but I know that we were exposed because we were below these buildings. So we were exposed to the fire. But there was sniper fire, there was infantry fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So the answer is yes, you did come under sniper fire from those buildings. Is that correct? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And did your side, that is, did your armed forces return sniper fire with sniper fire, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just told you a moment ago, we had no snipers at all. And we could not return sniper fire since we didn't have them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am not asking about your company, sir. I am asking whether, to your knowledge, sniper fire was returned --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is a belated objection, but I have to come back to the question: Did your side and so on return sniper fire with sniper fire? The witness just said a moment ago that they had no snipers. Now, putting these words in his mouth becomes a very nasty habit of the Prosecution. Now, this is not according to the Rules, and this is not right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, page 23, line 22, says "I don't know. I really don't know. I don't know if there were any at all because I was at this line here and there were none. I am sure of that." That seems to be an answer to your last question or do I --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I think there is a difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask the witness to take his headphones off. Could you explain the difference to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: This question -- this question canvases whether this witness, company commander of that part of the front line directly opposite those high-rise buildings was aware of sniper fire being returned with sniper fire from the forces of the SRK in that area. It does not re-activate the issue of whether there was snipers in his particular company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but, I think you asked more you asked more than just snipers in his particular company. You asked about snipers in the Ilidza Brigade, not just in his company.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Earlier I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "I don't know. I really don't know. I don't know if there was any at all." So I understand this to be within the brigade and he was at the line there. Let me ask one question to the witness. Could the witness please put the headphones again. Mr. DP6, one of the earlier questions was about snipers in the -- or sniper activity in the Ilidza Brigade; you said you didn't know about it. Would you know about snipers in the Sarajevo Romanija Corps? So not necessarily part of the brigade you were in with your company.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I really don't know about the Sarajevo Romanija Corps having any snipers. If I don't know about the Ilidza Brigade, how could I know about the SRK?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps I could speak first.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace asked first. Please, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Present, I do wish to proceed this line of questioning. If you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want to explain, then we rather ask the witness to put his earphones off again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Or perhaps leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I asked him yesterday whether he understood any English or French, and since these are the only languages used, unless you say there is another way of perceiving the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I would prefer for my part, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, would you please. May I ask you to leave the courtroom just for one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. President. This -- the proceedings of this morning, the objections by my learned colleague, raise a fundamental issue in relation to the nature of cross-examination, in particular, whether a cross-examiner is bound by the first answer of a witness on a relevant topic. In my respectful submission, the fact that the witness said he knows nothing about it, does not in itself mean that a cross-examiner should not ask further questions, if the cross-examiner -- if there is an issue between that answer and the case of the cross-examiner. Put simply, the Prosecution seeks to continue the line of questioning amongst other reasons, in order to probe the credibility of the witness on this issue. In relation to that, Mr. President, the situation is that he was

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: [redacted] immediately adjacent to the Institute for Blind Children. I hasten to add that that period of command ended in February 1993, and the three scheduled sniping incidents which occurred in a relatively short compass of that institute took place between March and June 1994 and, therefore, there is of course the possibility that snipers were operating from the institute in 1994, but not up until February 1993. Even so -- in my respectful submission, it is appropriate for the Prosecution to be permitted to pursue this line of questioning. It defies common sense to accept at least on the strength of one answer, or even a few answers, this witness's contention that he was not aware whether the SRK used snipers during this armed conflict, let alone, that there weren't snipers in his brigade. We know from the evidence of Richard Philipps, for instance, that there was a sniper squad within the Ilijas Infantry Brigade, and that was not challenged by the Defence, and that is the reason I say we know. It is not an issue. We know, similarly, that there were snipers in the SRK beyond that brigade using specialist rifles, and again we know that because it was never challenged. Mr. President, this is an important site of sniping and here we have [redacted] up until February 1993. With the caveat, with the proviso, that it is not the most relevant periods of time, even so, in my respectful submission, it would be appropriate to pursue it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, in French there is a very beautiful expression meaning "I am speechless," really. However, I will find some words to explain this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am a bit surprised that speechless, you surprise the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am hoping to continue to surprise you, Mr. President, because if the Defence had tried this brilliant style, I have to admit, to immediately question one of your decisions, immediately we would have been told "this is not admitted" either in one Chamber or else where. What is happening here? We have a witness who just told us -- I don't know, I haven't seen it, I don't know anything about it, as far as I know, there weren't any. Now, why? At all costs we want to find out that he should be placed, put in the place that he has to be interrogated inquisition style when he is continuing to answer "I don't know." Here is the testimony of the witness. Do you want him to tell you the opposite? To contradict himself, to perjure himself, to tell you lies? What do you want? What do you want him to say? I think the Prosecution needs to know, just like you, Mr. President, reminded us that this is a mixed system whereby the interpretation of proof will be done by you, not by us, but has to be respected what the witness said. Now, not only that I am speechless, I don't know what to say, when we were told that we never contested this, I have to remind you that expert Philipps was that someone that we considered as being an OTP staff member, that we did not think that his capacity as a witness was a good one. Of course, we contest the entire of his testimony. We cannot say that we admit something that we contest. That is not in the Rules. Therefore, the testimony of the witness is being very clear. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Now, having said on three separate occasions that he didn't know anything about it, it is completely abnormal that he continues to be asked leading, contentious questions: Did you return sniper fire with sniper fire when you were attacked in this way? I believe it is not admissible. If it is admissible, then the Defence rights are being offended. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, the Chamber has confirmed that there are two issues. One is receiving information from the witness; the second one is testing reliability and credibility of the witness. As far as receiving information from the witness, he has testified that he doesn't know anything about it. I think you asked questions several times on this issue, and the Chamber wonders what other questions could shed a further light on the issue you are pursuing, that is, credibility, reliability. If you could demonstrate that by your next question, but we have to limit that. I mean, even in the stage of credibility, reliability, we have to stop somewhere and we cannot ask the witness to deny seven, eight, nine, ten times.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if it assists, I don't propose to do that. That would be a complete waste of time. That is not the way to conduct cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What kind of questions would you then have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, yesterday, the witness said that it wasn't possible to say Ante Babica Street from the street of the blind. Hopefully, I will demonstrate to him you that that evidence is incorrect. An area that I propose to further explore is what was upstairs in the school for the blind. The witness told us yesterday one floor; in fact, it is ground plus two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we do not concentrate any more on sniper. One of the problems the Chamber had with your line of questioning as well is that the term "sniper" was used again where there seems, at least there seems to be some disagreement on what exactly a sniper is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And indeed my next few questions will break away from that, in relation to that term.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I just found my words again. I really don't see the connection between whether we have a view on such a street from such an institute with the question that raised my objection, "Did you return sniper fire with sniper fire?" There is no connection whatsoever. I don't think the Prosecution has understood the purpose of the cross-examination in the two systems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The line just indicated by the Prosecution is an admissible line. So, Mr. Ierace, we know exactly to what questions the witness has answered "no," and there is no need to have that repeated several times. But I cannot imagine that there are issues like the ones you mentioned you would like to raise. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To be perfectly clear on this, Mr. President, I also propose to ask him, well, [redacted]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher -- unless there is anything else you would like to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just a minor correction. I said earlier that the relevant scheduled incidents were in the first half of 1994. Incident 13 was on the 4th October, 1993, but that that doesn't change the argument I advance. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, would you please escort the witness into the courtroom, please. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will continue, Mr. DP6. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, when you had a sniper or snipers operating from those high-rise buildings opposite your part of the front line, what did you do in order to neutralise them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We would open fire towards these parts approximately from where the fire came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And would that be with semi-automatic rifles, as well as automatic rifles, as well as machine-guns?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Surely there were occasions when what you really needed was someone who had particular skill at using a rifle in order to neutralise a sniper on the other side. Did that situation not arise --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President. Mr. President, the question is now being asked --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could take his headphones off --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Excuse me? If you speak all at the same time, I cannot hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And I ask he remove his headphones

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, first of all, I would like to apologise for the Prosecution, because I reacted very rapidly, precisely so that the witness is protected. But currently what is happening here is that a question is again being asked about nothing else but the existence of snipers. But that are now being defined by a person who got has special qualities. Now, this is going around the pot really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is an admissible question, so the objection is denied. It is also reflects the line of questioning indicated by the Prosecution in the absence of the witness. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, you have told us that in order to neutralise snipers in those high-rise buildings, you would return fire. Were there not times -- were there not situations which called for one of your subordinates to -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The accused would like to confer with counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, would it assist if we took the break a little earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the observation that General Galic formulated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...to take his headphones off again. Would you take them off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it seems that the observation that I was given by General Galic is the following: It seems that this witness himself would never have used the term "sniper," and I don't have the recollection. I am just --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just finish, please, before objecting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it is simply not appropriate for the Defence to make submissions in these terms. If my learned colleague has an objection to the question, then he should make it, but not relate what has just been told by his client in a general way about the general issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to finish my sentence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...confer with your client, and you may submit whatever you want to this Chamber as a Defence, but it is the counsel that represent the accused. And so therefore, references to what is the source and what is the basis of your objection Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. should not link -- should not create an indirect way of addressing the Chamber. But, therefore, I think that your --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But could we ask the Prosecution to tell us the reference, precise reference, page and line, that the witness said that there was sniper fire that was coming from a high-rise flats, high-rise buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I can give that reference Mr. President, page 33, line 16 question asked by me: "When you had a sniper, were snipers operating from those high-rise buildings opposite of that part of your front line, what did you do in order to neutralise them." Answer: "We would open fire towards these parts approximately from where the fire came from."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Present, I noticed that you conferred with your client, and I also note that you wanted to object against something. If you would please keep the two strictly apart. Make your objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, with pleasure. What I think I can tell, I believe this is an interpretation problem because it seems that the same time General Galic and Ms. Pilipovic heard the witness say that he did not know, as far as he was concerned, whether it was one or the other. And it seems this cannot be found in the transcript, although both the General and Ms. Pilipovic can confirm this while I was listening to another channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness please put his headphones on again. Did we understand your well, Mr. DP6, that sniper fire came from high-rise buildings at the other side of the confrontation line, or is this a wrong understanding of what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the other side, fire was open, both sniper and infantry fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is an answer to my question. Please proceed -- no. We will -- no. I would like to you to know even for the last two minutes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you received sniper fire from those high-rise buildings, [redacted], [redacted]-- I withdraw that -- someone with the skill of a marksman to take them out, to eliminate them?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why don't we first -- yes, make your objection, Mr. Piletta-Zanin but let me be quite clear. Questions are put to a witness in order to get an answer. Questions are not put to a witness in order to give an opportunity on each question to object. Make your objection and think it over what I just said during the next break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will do it. Yes, I will do it. The formulation of the objection is because it is purely speculative because we are being told --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Headphones for the witness, please, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please take off your headphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is purely speculative. The witness is being asked whether if he wished to have someone, why is he not asked did call someone, then it would be a lot clearer. Is it: Would you have wished to have had someone? This is purely speculative. This is talking about a desire he may have had. Now, the Defence is always asked to be precise, now we are asking the other side to be accurate. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I did understand the question of -- in such a way whether the witness ever had felt the need to find someone, and that is a perfectly acceptable interpretation of this question. But I will put it to the witness in these terms, and that will be the last question before the break. Mr. DP6 could you -- when you received sniper fire from the other side of the line, have you ever felt the need to find someone with special skills to respond to that fire or to eliminate the sniper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let me tell you: Anyone would have wanted to eliminate the sniper, but what can I tell you? I couldn't have wished because when the fire started, I wouldn't know whether this was sniper fire or this was some other infantry fire, fire from infantry weapons. You just wish that you could eliminate fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then again my question, whether sniper or infantry fire, did you ever try to find someone or to eliminate those who were at the source of the fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, when the fire was opened, first of all, the attempt would be to eliminate fire from the front line. If that is not possible, we would call the battalion command and then we would say on this part this fire being opened. And we would ask for assistance so that the fire would be then eliminated in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you ask for that assistance, what then happens?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, then we would be sent either soldiers as reinforcement to come and deal with it, or they would start to make sure that a shell would fall or something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, 30 seconds only to tell you that Mr. Aleksandar Momirov, who is our case manager, will also be present at the hearing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, then please proceed. Welcome into the courtroom, Mr. Momirov. May I first ask you to spell your name so that there can be no confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOMIROV
utterances.text: M-o-m-i-r-o-v. Yes, thank you. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, you told us before the break that when you wanted to eliminate fire from the front line, whether it was sniper fire or some other form of fire, you would call the battalion command and ask for assistance. Firstly, when you called the battalion command, would you use a field telephone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And you explained that the assistants would either be soldiers as reinforcement or they would start to make sure that a shell would fall or something like that. Do you mean that sometimes the assistance was artillery fire against the source of fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whereabouts were the artillery units that would operate opposite your part of the front line up until February 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mortars were down next to the Theological Faculty.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were there also mortars at the old JNA barracks at that period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Only at the Theological Faculty as far as the area of Nedzarici. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What size were those mortars or what sizes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 60, the 82, and the 120.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Merely one part of the witness's answer has not been interpreted into French. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you look at the screen, in English it is complete. Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You have told us that the mortars were at the Theological Faculty. Did you sometimes receive the assistance of artillery shells rather than mortars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you sometimes receive the assistance of tanks coming into Nedzarici to assist you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am really sorry, but I would like to be very precise. You are talking about the tank and I think that in French it -- the French interpretation was "guns." Now, could we please be very precise here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am not an expert but as far as I understand tanks are usually translated by chars. Could this be confirmed by the French -- no, of course, I should -- yes. Yes. Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I wonder if it would assist if we can have the same rules of translation issues as applied during the Prosecution case, that a note be made of them so as to minimise the amount of interruptions of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, since you noticed the difference, you have the original language and you have the French. So would you use the small yellow papers if there is any need that the translation be adjusted, or at least if you have any submissions to be made in respect of translation, at least if no confusion could arise. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Might the witness be shown Exhibit P3279T.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is a series of six photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: ERN ending in three small "a."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you going to -- it is a series of six. Do you have one -- yes, you have the ERN number mentioned of the photograph you wish on the ELMO. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, in the photograph before you, do you see the Theological Institute otherwise known sometimes as the School of Theology?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please point to it with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness indicates a white building of which at least three floors can be seen about two-thirds up the photograph from the bottom. Thank you. Might that be returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, when you contacted the battalion headquarters, I take it that is the headquarters that you placed on the map, that you indicated on the map yesterday. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I take it there were a number of battalions in the Ilijas Brigade. What was the name of that battalion? Was it the 1st Battalion, the 2nd Battalion, or what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you told us the various battalion commanders. Who was the battalion commander as of the 13th of July, 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I returned, then it was Svetozar Guzina, after I returned from the spa. And then onward it was Svetozar Guzina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you know him personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met him when I returned from the spa.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was that the first time you had met him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know whether he had previously been in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he wasn't -- I mean, he did his military service as everybody else, but he wasn't an active JNA member.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know if he is still alive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know where he lives? I am not asking you for the address, but simply if you know where he lives. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If you had to locate him, do you know people who may know?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object. And I do not see the relevance. It looks to me a little bit like a fishing expedition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, should the headphones be taken off?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please take your headphones off, yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the relevance is an exhibit in the Prosecution case that was tendered through [redacted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will make that redaction. At the same time, the knowledge of the witness on the whereabouts was the relevance for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The relevance for that is to establish whether the Defence wished to do it so that they could contact him if they wish to refute that if you wish to do so. It is P2759, confidential exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence does not intend to communicate with that person, rest assured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that take away the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then please proceed. But this was about the address. So the objection is of, at least, the whereabouts and whether the witness knows anything about that. But of course the -- well, not of course, but the Prosecution has demonstrated sufficiently the relevance of the other part of the question, so please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, you told us that sometimes the battalion would provide you with reinforcements. What skills did those reinforcements have when you were concerned about -- when you wanted to eliminate sniper and other fire from the other side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had no training and the skill amounted to what we learned in the war, and reinforcements were sent over from other front lines, that is from other companies -- I mean, human reinforcements, troop reinforcements.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The mortar placements at the Theological Institute, did you ever see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When was the first time approximately that you saw them, and the last time that you saw them, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately the first time I saw them, sometime in June, and the last time - I don't remember - could have been sometime before I was wounded. I really -- I really don't remember when the last time was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether the last time you saw them was sometime after October 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were down there where they had always been.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And were they in exactly the same positions whenever you saw them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, sir the front line around Nedzarici was such that it could be described perhaps as a spur. In other words, Nedzarici was surrounded on three sides by positions of the ABiH. Would you regard that as an accurate description?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We could only get out -- we had only one exit to one side, and that was via Kasindolska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To the south of Nedzarici was a similar protrusion for the enemy, that is, the area of Dobrinja. Is that correct? In other words, there were -- Dobrinja was an area of ABiH territory which was surrounded on three sides by the SRK, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object. I object, Mr. President. I do not know -- perhaps the witness could remove his headset. I object to the question because it is imprecise. We know that there is an exact number for the Dobrinja and we know about it. The certain areas were surrounded by the so-called army of Sarajevo, but other parts of Sarajevo -- of Dobrinja were controlled by different troops. Now, the question is not precise. It introduces confusion and, therefore, in compliance with the Rules, the Prosecution should make the question precise, should word it precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ierace, if you are talking about Dobrinja, the evidence is until now that Dobrinja was split, that parts of it were under the control. So if -- may I take it - and perhaps you could be more precise - that you are speaking about certain parts of Dobrinja, and I would have another question myself. You are placing Dobrinja south of Nedzarici which is in my maps not evident. I would say it was rather east or perhaps -- or am I wrong? What I find on my maps just south of the area known to me as Nedzarici is what is what we call the Airport Settlement --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the parts you are referring to are rather to the east or to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: South-east.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, there were areas of Dobrinja

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness does not have the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please -- yes. You know already perfectly well how to do it, Mr. DP6. Thank you for your cooperation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, a large part of the settlement of Dobrinja controlled by the ABiH. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And the part that was controlled by the ABiH was surrounded on three sides by - if not almost on four sides - forces of the SRK. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Before I give you an opportunity to object, I hear from my place with my earphones on that you communicate in your own language which is understandable for the witness. That is not allowed in this courtroom. If you want to confer, no problem. One of the reasons might be that if you have got your headphones on, that you have more difficulties in hearing each other, therefore, you use a louder voice. But it is not admissible to speak -- especially not if even with my limited knowledge of the B/C/S language, I could hear what your view on that question would be, and it is up to the witness to tell us. If there is any objection, then may I ask you to take off your earphones again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I withdraw the question.
