utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. I note the frequently --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I merely would like to bring you my apologies. Yes, perhaps, we are too loud but we shall pay attention not to do that again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, does that mean that my learned colleague does not object to the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I thought that Mr. Ierace was about to rephrase his question --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will withdraw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- or was it a misunderstanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The settlement of Dobrinja --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, the settlement of Dobrinja was, I think you have agreed already, in part controlled by the ABiH, as far as the armed conflict was concerned. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with Ante Babica Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ante Babica, it is in Mojmilo, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And that was one of the -- indeed, that was the main road which connected the ABiH controlled part of Dobrinja to the parts of the city that were controlled by the ABiH. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Essentially, that street was the main connection road between Dobrinja and the city in terms of the ABiH territories. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All I know is that it was towards Mojmilo where the Ante Babica Street extended out, I don't know. I know that it went to Mojmilo -- not Mojmilo, but Vojnicko Polje and you know how the road takes you on then. But Mojmilo is one thing, and Vojnicko is another. I am not really very familiar with that part of Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If I understand your evidence, are you telling us that you do not know whether Ante Babica was a road within the control of the ABiH during the war which was a main connection between the city and the territories they controlled in Dobrinja? Are you saying you do not know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that Ante Babica was controlled by the BH army, but I don't know where is the beginning and where is the end of that street. I don't know how long is that street. Because a moment ago you mentioned Dobrinja. You said that Ante Babica started in Dobrinja and then that it went on to, what is it, Vojnicko Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Let me rephrase the question. Are you aware that if you wished to travel in those years to the ABiH held part of Dobrinja, that one from the city that the road -- that road I mentioned, Ante Babica, could be used in order to make that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I must object here. On the one hand, it is highly hypothetical question and cannot be answered because this road was controlled by the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you wanted to go from the city to the ABiH controlled part of the Dobrinja, would you have to take Ante Babica to get there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time, I couldn't do that. I couldn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For someone who would be on the other side of the confrontation line, would he have to take that road to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To get to Dobrinja, he wouldn't have to, no. He wouldn't have to take that route because there was another route via Srakino Selo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which one was that? Can you point to that on the map. Could perhaps the map can be placed on the ELMO again. Can you indicate what other --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Lukavicka Cesta, from here, and one could get to the city this way, or one could go to the tram stop which is Ante Babica Street. But Lukavicka Cesta -- Lukavicka Cesta, that is what this street is called up to this point. From here to this place and it takes you through Nedzarici. But you could also get into the city below Mojmilo, that is, take Lukavicka Cesta, then take around here, I think all this way, and then you get into the city.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if you would go to the city, you would either turn right on to Ante Babica or continue until the tram stop? Is that how I understand your -- there were two ways --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, two. This is Lukavicka and then you get do Ante Babica until you reach the tram stop or rather the tram tracks. But you can go below Mojmilo hill and then via Srakino Selo, Olimpijska, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I want to be very precise so that we avoid any future doubts. The witness said in his language, I think he said that he thought that he believed that the street could take you as far as a particular point, but he wasn't quite sure. That is, he was not at all sure whether the street ended there, and I want the transcript to reflect that. I believe that is what I heard in his language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, having regard to the features of the map that you have just shown us, whether you came down Ante Babica Street or whether you came down Salida Hadzic [sic] Street, ultimately you ended up bottom of Mojmilo hill into area of Lukavicka Cesta. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You would end up in Lukavicka Cesta, that's where you would get to. Because I think it goes here -- I don't know. I think it goes here towards Nedzarici and there towards Lukavicka. Ante Babica Street, this street goes straight towards the tram station.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, please stop there for a moment. The point is this: That the part of the front line that you controlled was immediately opposite a tactically important supply route for the ABiH. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In which part?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the map in front of you, yesterday you marked the part of the front line that was under control of your forces, that's the continuous black line.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Opposite that line, not immediately opposite, but a little further back, you have Ante Babica Street and you also have the street that runs along the bottom of Mojmilo, Salida Hadjic [sic]. And they were important supply routes for the ABiH into Dobrinja. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes. They had to go through here, yes, to get to Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And at the time that you were in command, you appreciated that fact, didn't you? In other words, you knew the significance of the territory not far from your front line. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I will repeat the question. At the time that you were in command, you knew the significance of the territory, that is, the territory of the ABiH not far from the front line controlled by your forces under your command, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew that they used that route to get to Dobrinja, to Dobrinja V, in fact, to the whole of Dobrinja, which was under their control.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But this street was blocked.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It wasn't possible to see the street in that part, this part here. This part you couldn't see. There were screens and containers. It wasn't possible to see in this part here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, for the purpose of the record, you indicate the portion of Ante Babica between Salida Hadjica and Lukavicka Cesta. Is that correct? You say that that part wasn't visible?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is pointing to a different street --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will take care of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please point at the part of Ante Babica Street, that part which is at the right-hand side we find the word "Mojmilo," near to a street Olimpijska, and on the left-hand side, whether there is a red cross and a rectangular structure in the map. When the witness earlier pointed at a place where the tram stop would be, he was pointing to the crossroad immediately below where the words "Bitu Menka" appears on the map. When the witness indicated another road that could be used to go to Dobrinja, he was pointing at Salida Hadjica Street, which is parallel to what is called on the map Boulevard Mese Selimovica. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence apologises for interrupting during the questions of my learned colleague, but we would just like to know considering the examination-in-chief, since it lasted less than two hours we think, we would like to ask how long our learned colleague is going to go on so that we have another five witnesses who would like to resolve this issue. And the Defence would like to agree, if that is all right, in order not to lose time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Defence stressed again and again that I should account "net" time instead of "total" time. Of course I have been wondering whether I should draw attention of the Prosecution to the time limits. Usually I would do that, but if I have to count net time, I would have great difficulties. That is not to say that I do not ask the Prosecution to proceed and see whether they conclude as soon as possible, but my earlier remarks might shed some light as to the -- how this examination of this witness developed. And, therefore, I expect an indication soon now from Mr. Ierace to hear how much time he would still need, and to see whether we can proceed as efficiently and as quickly as possible. And this is for both parties. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, it follows that any part of the territory under your personal command in that period --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there was a question that was addressed to the Prosecution. We asked him to find out how much more time they needed, and the Prosecution didn't answer. And we would like to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I asked the Prosecution to give an indication soon as to how much time they would need. The reason why I did so is that if you would like to have this kind of information, you do not ask for it in the middle of a question, but you wait until a suitable moment where you change subject or whatever. So I invited the Prosecution -- let me just find my words -- "I expect an indication soon now from Mr. Ierace to hear how much time he would still need." So I left it up to him to find a suitable moment. So apart from listening to your own questions, perhaps you could also listen to the -- what I asked from the Prosecution. This is a waste of time, the way we proceed. I am not talking about the subject. And the Chamber will consider what to do in order to make this better, but, first of all, urges the parties to cooperate in that respect. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Therefore, any part of that route that could be seen from the area under your control was particularly observed by your forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This part of the road -- I said it a moment ago. This part of the road was protected by screens and containers, and you were not able to see --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am not asking you for the parts you couldn't see. And at this stage, I am not asking you for the parts that you could see. I am simply putting to you that it was of great significance to you as the commander to keep a watchful eye on whatever parts you could see. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct. But this was protected. Every part of the road that could possibly be visible from the area of Nedzarici was protected in that part.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, obviously the reason that you would want to observe that route is if the opportunity presented itself, you could hit any legitimate targets that might go between the city and Dobrinja, the area held by the ABiH. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We tried to have as little traffic as possible between Dobrinja and the city --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- because of the BH army and their attacks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really apologise, but I think that this type of question precisely is not on, because the witness already answered because the interest of seeing the road, the interest of seeing a road -- sorry. Could you please. Thank you. Thank you very much, Mr. Ierace. Now, the interest of seeing, having a view of the route is also being protected oneself in terms if there is an attack. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, of course this question is leading, and you could have -- I could have asked whether the importance of the road was to count the density of traffic for future route planning. You could -- it is the question of the Prosecution. It has got nothing to do with the one and only logical explanation, it is just the suggestion put by the Prosecution in this question to the witness, and that is perfectly admissible. Of course, you could have asked in cross-examination [sic] to ask whether the importance of the road was for whatever other reason, but this is the question of the Prosecution. It is leading the witness, and it is intentionally leading the witness and there is no reason not to admit that question. So may I ask you and not for the first time today to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to be reticent and, of course, this is not to deny you the right to object, of course not. Please continue, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Might that exhibit be withdrawn for the moment and the witness shown P327900, which is a bundle of photographs, in particular photograph ending with -- photograph ending with the numbers "08." Just while that is being done, a question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If you did have a place that gave you a view of the -- yes -- a view of the -- those routes, you would have taken advantage of it in terms of insuring that you could fire from that position. Is that correct? If there had been such a place, and I appreciate you say there was not such a place.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, look at the photograph in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could the ELMO be panned back so we can all see.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence apologises. I believe that that question was a hypothetical one asked by my learned colleague, unless they are admissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the question could be put in a non-hypothetical way, although hypothetical questions sometimes -- oh, yes. The question has already been answered. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I just say, you haven't heard me on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I appreciate the answer has been given. For future reference, in my respectful submission, there is nothing wrong about a hypothetical question in those circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it depends on the circumstances. That is the issue, I would agree with you. Sometimes hypothetical questions should not be admissible, sometimes they would be. Perhaps at a later stage, we could perhaps once discussed with the parties a bit more about what questions are admissible and what are not. Since the question has been answered, please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, does this photograph appear to be taken from the Institute for Blind Children looking towards those routes that we talked about a few minutes ago, and demonstrating that those routes could not be seen in relation to these buildings in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This could not have been taken from the Institute for Blind Children. This could only have been taken from the part of Lukavicka up, upon -- up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What do you mean by "Lukavicka up"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I meant to say is that it could not have -- the photograph could not have been taken from the Institute for Blind Children. The Institute for Blind Children is on the Aleja Branka Bujica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I suggest to you that, in fact, this is the view which you have, that is, one part of the view that you have from one of the Institute for Blind Children buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that the witness was already asked twice and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Under the circumstances, in view of the evidence, the -- Mr. Ierace may proceed. The objection is denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I suggest to you that in fact this photograph, that is, the view which you can see in the photograph, indicates that it was taken from one of the buildings in the Institute for Blind Children. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I say it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Are you able to suggest, assuming it was taken from a building, where it was taken from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness -- I withdraw that. Before the photograph is taken away. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The building which appears in the foreground, perhaps you could point to it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No. Bring the pointer further down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Lower the pointer by about 3 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. A bit further down. A bit forth down, please. Could you please bring the pointer a little further down. Thank you. Do you recognise that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Before the war began, did you live in Nedzarici -- and I am not asking you whereabouts -- but did you live in Nedzarici? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For how many years did you live there before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war, from 1970.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: [redacted] have indicated on the map. You tell us that you don't recognise that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember this part here. This building, this building here and this part I remember. But this, this, I can't remember. I can't remember what it is. It is a car park or something. I don't know what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the purpose of the record, the witness has indicated all the high-rise buildings as buildings he recommends, but not the construction which appears in the middle left of the photograph. Might that photograph be taken away but shown photograph with ERN ending with number "11." Perhaps when you return, Madam Usher, you could take the earlier photograph with you, so that we can have both on the ELMO, if required. I am sorry -- yes, thank you. At this stage, please place photograph 11 on the ELMO, ending in number "11." No, that is not the photograph. No. I will show you the photograph. It might help. Would you find that one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: What number is that, please, Mr. Ierace? This exhibit has only two photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: My apologies. Excuse me. That is P327900.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it be double "N" perhaps? No, it might not be. That is another series.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Double zero --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Double zero has two photographs only?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could hold them up. It could save some time. It is neither of those. Perhaps we could try double N. Yes, double N, my apologies. So P3279NN, which should be a bundle of photographs.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: A set of two photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you hold them up so the witness can't see them. Yes, the top one. And please place that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, in this photograph, do you the same building in the foreground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, you are now pointing to it. And having regard to the view, do you now recognise that both of these photographs are, in fact, taken from one of the buildings of the Institute for Blind Children? In other words, this photograph is looking slightly to the left of the other photograph taken from the same place.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you please, this is Lukavicka Cesta here. Is that correct? Let me have a look. This here these are student hostels over there. This is the Lukavicka Cesta, and it goes up here, and here is the intersection up to here. And the Institute for Blind Children, the Institute for Blind Children would be about here. And you cannot photograph --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would the ELMO please pan back so we can see all of the photograph and in particular to where the witness just pointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, would you point again to where you said the Institute for Blind Children is. I think you pointed to the left of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These student hostel buildings and here would be the Institute for Blind Children, all the way there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I would like to witness to be shown another photograph. P3279OA.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, first of all, please point to the student hostel, I think you called it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The hostels, yes, the student hostels, please point to those buildings.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there a second student hostel building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you point to that as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, in this photograph, do you see Ante Babica Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ante Babica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you having trouble in finding --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The witness indicates the road that runs parallel to the bottom of the photograph and is immediately above the bottom of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, do you see --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now, wait a moment. This ought to be Ante Babica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. All right, now, do you see in the top left-hand corner the buildings of the Institute for Blind Children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, do you see that two of the buildings appear to face towards the camera, that is, the two on the right, whereas the one on the left appears to face away to the left of the photograph, so that it is at an angle to the camera. I am talking about the buildings of the Institute for Blind Children.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you come to the building on the far left, that is, the Institute for Blind Children building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. And so as we look at that building, it is at an angle to the camera, do you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, yesterday we saw that building consisted of ground floor and then two rows of windows above the ground floor. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, I suggest to you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see two.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I suggest to you that the two photographs I showed you a few minutes ago were taken from the top level of that building towards the corner closest to the camera in this photograph. I am not saying that you know that. What I am saying to you is that the view which those photographs showed is what you would expect to see from that angle of the top floor of that building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry. Could I have the photograph again.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I merely want to say that the witness has answered, I believe, three times this question when it comes to taking photographs from that building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That last question was not -- could we just -- it is not clear exactly to the Chamber. Could you please take your headphones off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask something, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know well where Jugobanka was and I know well where that building is. And nobody can talk me out of what I do know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No one is talking you out of anything at all. Would you please take your headphones off for just a second. Yes. Thank you. Mr. Ierace, the -- you are asking the witness at this moment to identify the place from where a photograph was taken. Is his awareness of specifically that place, is there any necessity to establish this, because it creates a lot of confusion, if you might have noticed. And I wonder whether it is the spot in the city that creates confusion, because it is not the first time, especially on these photographs, we had huge confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Would it assist you, Mr. President, if I was to explain in the absence of the witness and perhaps in private session very quickly where all this is going.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I -- could I ask the witness to leave the courtroom for one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No -- yes, you have your earphones on. Could you please follow the usher for a couple of minutes to leave the courtroom. Yes. We will turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, if you would escort the witness into the courtroom, we will turn into open session again. We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP6, you had to wait a little bit longer. I hope you got some copy. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, before we -- before you left the courtroom, I had suggested to you that the two photographs I showed you earlier, that is, the view in those photographs was consistent with them being taken from the building of the Institute for Blind Children, which appeared at the top of aerial-type photograph. And you asked us if you could see again those first two photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown both the aerial photograph, which is P3279OA, and also the two earlier photographs, which are P327900, ERN ending in "08," and P3279NN, with an ERN ending in number "11." So that is three photographs altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you receive those photographs, please look at them and consider your answer. As you consider your answer, I will point out the feature to you. In one of the three photographs, you can see a drainpipe in the top left-hand corner. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the record, that is number "11." I will refer to it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That is a drainpipe for taking water off a roof. I think you are holding that photograph at the moment and you are pointing to the drainpipe. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we have the photograph on the ELMO, please, so that we can follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please place that photograph on the ELMO. Thank you. And I think you may conclude from that that the photograph was taken looking sideways along a wall and from an opening immediately under the roof. You might look again at photograph P3279OA, that is the aerial-type photograph, and consider what I said to you earlier, that the view in the other two photographs is consistent with them being taken from the upper level of the white building on the left.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This photograph --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the microphone be brought closer to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This photograph here, had it been taken from the home of blind children and it had been taken in the direction of Lukavicka Cesta, then you would first see the shopping centre and you wouldn't be able to see the student hostel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Would you please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just intervene. Because the witness seems to understand your question, as if the photograph was taken in the direction of Lukavicka Cesta. Perhaps could you first clarify that, because there seems to be some misunderstanding in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I intended to do that, Mr. President, by taking the witness to -- that's all right -- taking the witness to Exhibit D1760, that is the map. That might be the easiest way to clarify it. Please place that map on the ELMO. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, would you please indicate again on the map in front of you the position of those three buildings of the Institute for Blind Children.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is this here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The witness indicates --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And here, sorry. May I say something now?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the home for blind children. This is where the shopping centre is. Those buildings are here. In this part, these buildings could have been photographed from somewhere here because the students' hostel, if you can see the students' hostel too, or one wing of the hostel -- one wing of the hostel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. First of all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Ierace. Could I just ask you, because we have been talking about the institute and the shopping centre, et cetera. Maybe we should mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but then we would need other pictures because these are exhibits already admitted into evidence. So we would have to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I am talking of the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the map, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please point again to the buildings which are the Institute for Blind Children, whereabouts on the map would those three buildings be.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please take the blue pen and circle the position of the three buildings.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, above that, above the blue circle, put the letters "IBC."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, take the pointer, not the pen, and point to where the shopping centre was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The shopping centre is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, tell us what the shopping centre looked like during the conflict. How many storeys was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No storeys at all. The shopping centre -- the shopping centre had a ground floor and a roof above it, because it was ten years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, perhaps since the usher has the photographs -- please wait -- in her hand, at this stage on the top of the photograph, could you put photograph 11. You have only got the one photograph. I think it is on the table. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, that white building in the foreground, could you please point to it with the pointer. No. No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the students' hostel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, stop. Bring your pointer to the right, more to the right. Thank you. A little lower. Bring the pointer down. Thank you. Is that building the shopping centre? If you take your hand away, you can see all of the building. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This seems to be a part of the shopping centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, please, if the court usher could remove the photograph. And on the map, sir, with a cross, please mark the position of the shopping centre.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, alongside the cross in small letters, could you write the initials "SC."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you point to the two buildings which are the student hostels. Don't mark anything yet, just point to them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is one wing of the hostels.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, and can you see the other wing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can see all three of them here on the map, on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were there two separate buildings which were the students' hostels, each building having three wings each?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that is what I am saying. Wings, I can see all three wings of the hostels on the map -- excuse me. If this here is the Institute for Blind Children and over there the student hostels and this here is shopping centre, then what kind of a photograph could you take to cover all these places? And I remember very well this building here, this building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right. Yes, this building and that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Stop a minute. We can't see. Can you place the photograph on the ELMO. Sorry. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. DP6, if you want to point at something, first ask the usher to put that photograph on the -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, a minute ago you said, "I remember very well this building here." Please point to the building that you had in mind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is this building here and this building there. This building was before in front of Lukavicka Cesta, this here. This is alongside Lukavicka Cesta here. And in this passage here, it was the Jugobanka, bank building. Here is Lukavicka Cesta, here is the shopping centre, and here this didn't exist at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please stop for a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't know that we can make much sense of that for the transcript, but essentially the witness pointed first to a high-rise building with a whitish wall facing the camera above the building he earlier indicated may be the shopping centre. And he then indicated some high-rise buildings above the red roof. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the -- this is the shopping centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please wait for the question. Would you now please go -- I am sorry, you just indicated the building you said was the shopping centre. Could you place the pointer back on that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness indicates a building with a brown roof immediately to the right of the photograph of the roof which is coloured black, red, and orange in stripes. Please, court usher if you could remove that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, now on the map, can you circle the two student hostels, with your blue pen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Above them, would you please write the letters "SC" -- I am sorry "SH." On the road, if you just write "SH."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, please put down your pen and continue to look at the map. I want you to imagine, looking at the map, that you are standing in the position of the buildings of the Institute of Blind Children and facing towards the student hostel. In that position, you would have a road curving in front of you and to the right of the road, you would see the shop centre. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. You would also have on your immediate right --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But at the same time --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please wait for the question. On your immediate right, you would have a road going off to the right. Do you understand what I am putting to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is Aleja Branka Bujica which goes towards the students' hostels, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If you are looking toward the student hostel, that road would appear going in the direction of the student hostel. I am now talking about the road which would be to your immediate right going towards the south-east. Please point to that road, from the student hostel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. And the name of that road is? What is the name of that road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Lukavicka Cesta.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Excuse me. Now, I want you to look at photograph number 11 alongside the map. Position the photograph so you can move your eyes from the photograph to the map. Now, hypothetically accept from me for the moment that the photographer is standing in the position of the Institute for the Blind looking to the right of the student hostels. Do you understand what I am putting to you? Do you understand what I have just said? Please don't comment yet. So the photographer is standing in the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. You did not understand. Imagine that the photographer at the time he took this photograph was standing in the position of the Institute for Blind Children, in particular, in the position of the building closest to the road. Do you understand what I am putting to you? In other words, just --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You would expect that in the photograph on the left-hand side of the photograph you would see part of the student -- at least part of the student hostel complex, correct, if he was looking in that direction? You would expect that, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Look at the photograph. Do you see to the left of the photograph part of the student hostel complex?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, these are student hostels.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Look again at the map, please. You would expect to the right you would see Lukavicka Cesta and not so far to the right, you would see the shopping complex, do you agree? Looking at the map, that is what you would expect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the Institute for Blind Children, if you took the photograph, if you photographed this part and these buildings, because I can see these buildings next to the student hostel. These buildings next to -- next to the student hostel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please wait. Can the ELMO pan back so we can see the photograph. Further. Could you please repeat what you just said so that we can all now see the photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the student hostel. These are the buildings down there by the tram station.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Stop there, please. Go back to the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am going to make an objection because the witness wanted to say something and -- the witness wanted to say what one could see according to him, and he was interrupted by Mr. Ierace, who has been leading him in an unacceptable manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I simply wish the witness to indicate on the map where the tram station is because he hasn't done that yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That might be your next question. When you were interrupted, Mr. DP6 -- yes. When you were interrupted, what would you add? You told us about the buildings --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to say -- I wanted to say that in my opinion, it is impossible -- it is impossible that if then the closest thing would be to the photographer would be the -- if you are taking from the institute -- you would be -- for blind children, you would be looking at the shopping centre and that would be the closest. But if I am looking at it now, that is not so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Ierace, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the map, can you point to the position of the tram station that you mentioned a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here you are. This way here, this part here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, what is the name of that road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This road?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, what is its name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It says here Bolevar Mese Selimovica. This road goes through the city and next to this road is the tram station, you just cross the intersection and you get to the tram section. The tram is going from Bascarsija to Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Okay, now on that road we see a line in the middle which I think we can take as represent the tram line. Alongside the name "Oslobodjenje," we see a circle. Does that circle -- is the position of that circle where there was a turning mechanism for the tram, to turn them around? Where they stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This here where it says Bitu Menka and perhaps 50 metres from Bitu Menka, that's where you turn the tram around and not where the circle is by the Oslobodjenje building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the direction of the student hostels, that is where it should be, about here. This is where the tram turns around, not over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, are you saying that you would expect to see in the photograph in front of you that tram station? Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From -- if you look from this angle where it was photographed, you cannot see the tram stop, the tram station. What I am saying, you cannot see the tram station from there, because the tram station is behind the student hostels.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please indicate on the photograph again. Please give your answer again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The tram station is behind the student hostels.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So why do you say you would expect to see the tram station, if it is behind the students' hostels?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that I would expect to see a tram station, but I was just explaining to you that there is a tram station over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: You have told us that the Institute for Blind Children at the time that you were -- I will rephrase that -- up until February 1993, at least, was used on its upper floor as an observation point. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And I take it that you went there from time to time to see what you could observe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever see the tram station from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You cannot see the tram station from there. You can just see by the Oslobodjenje building where the tram goes. You can see the track, tram track, but you cannot see the station. It is Oslobodjenje building which is preventing you from seeing tram station from tram number five.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, if you can imagine standing in the observation level of the Institute for Blind Children, from there you could see going off to your right Lukavicka Cesta. Is that correct? Pardon my pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In front of you, you could see the shopping centre, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And in the distance to your left you could see the two student hostel buildings, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the left-hand side, I would have the student hostels on my left.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the photograph in front of you, consistent with that, you have identified part of the student hostel on your left, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can see one part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The student hostel -- I am sorry -- the shopping centre in front of you, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And going off to the right, can you see and identify Lukavicka Cesta?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Lukavicka Cesta.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No. I suggest to you that the other road is Lukavicka Cesta. Please point to the road going off to the right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. I suggest to you that that is Lukavicka Cesta.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In any event, do you agree that wherever this photograph is taken from is a position that, during the war, was on your side of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you agree that in this photograph -- I withdraw that. What have you referred to as the name of the road that ran from the Institute for Blind Children down to Ante Babica Street? What do you know that road's name to be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the Institute for Blind Children until Ante Babica Street, that was Aleja Branka Bujica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Aleja Branka Bujica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In this photograph, I suggest to you that in the distance towards the left we can see the intersection of Aleja Branka Bujica and Ante Babica immediately above the roof which is painted in black, red, and orange. Can you see that intersection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you like a magnifying glass? I have one here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As much as I think, it seems to me that this was taken from Lukavicka Cesta. It was photographed from Lukavicka Cesta, not from the Institute for the Blind. Because here is the shopping centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, that is not the question. I am asking you -- I am putting to you that in the photograph above the roof is an intersection, and I am suggesting to you it is the intersection of Lukavicka Cesta --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can see the street here. I can see the street here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask the witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But perhaps from some position from Lukavicka Cesta the photograph could have been taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask the witness be shown Exhibit P3279NN, with an ERN ending in numbers "09.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I want you to accept from me that this photograph is taken from the same place as the earlier photograph looking over the black, red, and orange roof, and in the direction of that same intersection. Do you now recognise that intersection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the Aleja here. Yes. The same as on the other photograph, except that this is -- the other one was further back. This was closer. That is that street and that is Ante Babica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I think you have agreed that from wherever this photograph was taken, it was somewhere on the territory that was controlled by the SRK, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I said that before, that it was taken from the territory of the SRK.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because on the Lukavicka Cesta -- from the Lukavicka Cesta was the SRK territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, more particularly, having regard to your identification of the shopping centre in photograph ending with the number 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And perhaps that could be placed back on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The photograph appears to be taken from somewhere in the area of the front line controlled by you and your fellow troops, that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, most probably. Because if it was taken -- if the photograph was taken from Lukavicka Cesta.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, assuming for the moment that the photograph was taken from a building which existed between the beginning of the conflict and February 1993, do you accept that indeed from buildings on your part of the front line you could see Ante Babica Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The street of Ante Babica, it was possible to see it from the buildings that we had, but until they put containers here and other things, some screens and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Do I understand you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But here you couldn't see anything when the war started, when they put barricades -- I don't mean barricades, containers. They put them there for their own protection, for their personal protection, so that they can move, so that people can move there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do I understand you to be agreeing that if not from the Institute for Blind Children, then certainly from other building on your part of the front line, you had a view of Ante Babica Street, except for the containers that were put up and other barricades?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you could have seen the Ante Babica Street, that is this intersection, from some parts. I don't know which ones. I don't know where this was taken from. But according to the picture, I can see that it was possible. And I know that during the war, there were containers here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, we don't have much time, so if you can sufficiently answer with a yes or no, if you can, please do so. Now, you have told us that containers and barricades were erected on that intersection. When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps it was a lapsus when I said barricades. I meant containers and protection of sorts. This was set up sometime -- I am not quite sure of the date -- but it was perhaps May, perhaps even before May in this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you point again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Do you mean May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, in spite of the containers or barriers -- I think the word you used was containers and --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think it is very important for the transcript that we indicate where was it that the witness indicated as having been the presence of containers, exactly on this part which was visible in the Serb territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, number one, we can't mark the photograph; secondly, that is an issue that could have been done in re-examination. But having said that, I am happy to, in the interest of saving time, to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I take it that the witness was referring to an intersection appearing on 3279NN, last two digits of the photo "11." In the left middle of the photograph which he testified was the same as on P3279NN, last two digits, "09," and there is only one intersection visible on that last photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you and your fellow troops do your best to hit legitimate military targets crossing that intersection, in spite of the containers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will rephrase it to make it easier. You have told us that there were some protective measures across that intersection, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And I assume that the purpose of those was to stop you and your fellow troops --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I am objecting to the -- in relation to the answer that was given by the witness. He -- according to him, his instruction was to return fire, that is what his testimony was earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...in the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There was nothing in the question that would exclude return fire, whatever kind of fire. It was just, apart from that, the testimony was broader. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, when you say that "there were protective -- protection that was erected," did you assume that to be at least visual protection for ABiH forces from observation by you and your fellow troops so that you couldn't see them, in other words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The protection was set up so that people can pass down the street because it was war. And civilians passed there as well as the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In spite of the protective measures, I suggest to you that fire continued into that intersection from your positions, the positions of you and your fellow troops.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the position where I was, personally, on the Lukavicka Cesta, you could not see this intersection. Because I was on the Lukavicka Cesta, you could only see it from the Aleja Branka Bujica where the Institute for Blind Children is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Will you please go back to the map P3279A. Sir, do you say that the Institute for Blind Children buildings were not part of the front line in your company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I said before. Only Lukavicka Cesta was part of my section of the front line. And you asked me about the Institute for the Blind, and the School of Theology, and the Centre for Blind People, and my answers were to those questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which company of your battalion had responsibility for those buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which buildings?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The Institute for Blind Children.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was the second company -- I am not quite sure. It was called the second company.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the second company from September of 1992 until August 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why, I don't know who was up to August 1994. I know that in the beginning it was Ljubo Cvijetic, he was the company commander, and there was one Slavko Orasanin until I was wounded. But then I don't know exactly who it was until the 24th. From the 19th of February, 1993, until August 1994, I don't know exactly who commanded the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is it therefore the case that you don't know whether there were snipers at any time between September 1992 and February 1993 operating from the Institute for Blind Children, since those buildings were outside the company where you operated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Earphones off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you take your earphones off, Mr. DP6. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, I think that we have come back again and again to the question of snipers. The witness has clearly indicated his position. And we were on a huge circle and now tell him were there snipers in his company, whereas he has very clearly testified on several occasions. If we want to respect the testimony, then let us do that, but I think that some rules ought to be respected. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness has repeatedly testified that he doesn't know anything about it, Mr. Ierace, so I don't think that this is of great use to continue. Please move to your next subject. And I indicated to you that you were expected to give us a time limit. And I know that the issue you are then dealing with took quite a long time, to put it in mild terms. Do you think you can finish in 10 minute approximately?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we have to consider whether more time will be granted to you. Perhaps we will stop in a couple of minutes to see what to do with that situation. Perhaps you finish the -- if there is any new question you would like to put to the witness now, you could do it; otherwise, perhaps we should discuss what the actual situation is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In view of the ruling Mr. President, I don't seek to ask any further questions of issue at this stage, and I would certainly seek clearance before I did in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the usher could please escort the witness out of the courtroom. But I might ask him to return to tell him what is going to help. So would you please leave the courtroom again for a couple of minutes, but stay standby. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would now like to turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the court schedule I saw that there has been no hearing planned for Friday next week. That was a bit of a surprise, because when the -- I am not talking about tomorrow, but I am talking about Friday next week. Because this has -- was not a decision of the Chamber. So, therefore, we still have to consider whether we will not sit next week Friday. Tomorrow, we will not sit because it is court maintenance. But next week Friday, that is a totally different matter. That is just to connect -- or at least Thursday is an UN holiday and for that reason, the Chambers were asked whether they would agree not to sit on Friday. Such agreement has not been given. So we will still consider that. The parties, therefore, could not rely specifically on the court calendar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, are you likely to reach a decision on that by this weekend?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will reach a decision by this weekend. I would say even today. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we are then going to have a serious problem for the Defence, because Ms. Pilipovic relied on this calendar. She already organised her trip to Belgrade. And your humble servant intended to benefit from this break and organise for himself a whole series of appointments in Geneva. I am just warning you that this can cause problems. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is good that you inform us. I was a bit surprised as well by the court calendar. I usually take it that apart from formal UN holidays and other court maintenance, that we will sit. And of course we will take into consideration that the court calendar might have confused you. Mr. DP6, unfortunately we could not conclude your testimony today. It will take presumably some time again not tomorrow, but early on Monday, because tomorrow this Chamber will not sit. It is very unfortunate that you have to stay for another few days, but would you be able to stay until next Monday? And I guarantee you that by next Monday it will be finished.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can stay because I have told people at the enterprise I work for that I perhaps stay -- Well, I thought I had finished on Friday and I thought I would be back on Monday, but I don't think it will be any difficulty. I will call them today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I feel very sorry for you that it takes so much time, and we highly appreciate that you can stay until next Monday. May I remind you not to speak to anyone the testimony you gave in this court. I hope to see you again Monday morning. We will adjourn until Monday morning, 9.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1.51 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 21st day of October, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
